rules.title: Prohibition on Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms for Residential Rentals
rules.requirement: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley, and unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords of residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley
rules.exemptions: Products that only aggregate and publish rental data anonymously, tools used to establish rent or income limits under affordable‑housing guidelines, and software used for market research, appraisal, or research/testing/training that does not use competitor data in the operational recommendation are excluded.
rules.quoted_span: A. It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.conflict_note: Ordinance does not specify an effective date; unclear if it takes effect upon adoption.
rules.interaction: Supersedes any prior local regulations on algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords may not inquire about, use, or base any rental advertising, application, tenant selection, lease terms, or termination decisions on a prospective or current tenant's criminal history. If a landlord takes any adverse action based on criminal history, they must provide written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental housing providers operating in the City of Berkeley
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties with limited exemptions; owner‑occupied properties (1‑3 units) where the owner resides; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Maximum Tenant Screening Fee
rules.requirement: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in Berkeley
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96
rules.interaction: Supersedes California Civil Code 1950.6(b) where the local cap is lower

rules.title: Prohibition of Non‑Refundable Fees for Existing Tenants
rules.requirement: An owner or the owner’s agent cannot charge a non‑refundable fee to any existing tenant for renewing a tenancy, including fees related to roommate changes.
rules.coverage_conditions: Existing tenants of residential rental properties in Berkeley
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.interaction: Supersedes any lease provision that permits such fees

rules.title: Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement Requirement
rules.requirement: Owners must provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and the maximum fee cap before receiving a screening fee from an applicant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents who charge a tenant screening fee in Berkeley
rules.quoted_span:
When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b)
rules.interaction: Imposes additional disclosure requirements beyond California Civil Code 1950.6

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment cap
rules.requirement: The Rent Board may not set the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) above 5% for any year.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully-covered rental units
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in the source text
rules.interaction: supersedes prior Berkeley Rent Ordinance AGA provisions

rules.title: Petitions limited to completed capital improvements
rules.requirement: Landlords may file rent‑increase petitions only for capital improvements that are completed, not for planned improvements.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords can only file a petition for rent increases for completed capital improvements (they can no longer petition to have rent increases preliminarily authorized for planned capital improvements).
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in the source text
rules.interaction: supersedes prior rule allowing petitions for planned improvements

rules.title: Nonpayment eviction threshold
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant for nonpayment only when the tenant owes at least one month’s Fair Market Rent for a comparable unit.
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in the source text
rules.interaction: adds a new just‑cause threshold to the existing nonpayment cause

rules.title: No eviction for failure to sign lease
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for refusing or failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed‑term lease expires.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in the source text
rules.interaction: removes a previously permissible eviction ground

rules.title: Just‑cause requirements for lease‑term violations
rules.requirement: Eviction for a lease‑term violation is allowed only if the violation concerns a mutually‑agreed term, causes substantial actual damage to the landlord, and the tenant’s behavior is unreasonable.
rules.quoted_span: Material lease terms only include mutually agreed upon lease terms. The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in the source text
rules.interaction: adds detailed just‑cause criteria to the existing lease‑violation eviction ground

rules.title: Maximum security deposit amount for most landlords
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge at most one month's rent as a security deposit for both unfurnished and furnished units.
rules.coverage_conditions: all landlords in Berkeley, except those meeting the small‑landlord exemption
rules.exemptions: landlords who own only two rental properties with ≤4 units and meet ownership criteria may charge up to two months' rent
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units
rules.interaction: supersedes state law where more protective

rules.title: Small‑landlord exemption for security deposit amount
rules.requirement: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, and whose ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC with all members natural persons, may charge up to two months' rent as a security deposit for both furnished and unfurnished units.
rules.coverage_conditions: landlords owning ≤2 properties and ≤4 residential units, ownership by natural person/family trust/LLC with natural‑person members
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or limited liability company (LLC) where all members are natural persons
rules.interaction: supersedes state law where more protective

rules.title: Photograph unit before or at start of tenancy
rules.requirement: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of the tenancy to document its condition.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.
rules.interaction: supersedes state law where more protective

rules.title: Return security deposit within 21 days
rules.requirement: All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned within 21 days after the tenant vacates the unit, with an itemized statement of deductions.
rules.quoted_span: All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned within 21 days after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant.
rules.interaction: supersedes state law where more protective

rules.title: Provide proof of repairs when returning deposit
rules.requirement: Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs were completed when returning the security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs were completed.
rules.interaction: supersedes state law where more protective

rules.title: 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order
rules.requirement: Landlords may increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026.
rules.coverage_conditions: eligible landlords with tenants whose tenancy began before January 1, 2025 and whose rents are not set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
rules.exemptions: Tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025, and rents set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act are exempt.
rules.quoted_span: At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026.
rules.interaction: Supersedes state rent increase limits for covered units; aligns with Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76.110A

rules.title: Rent Control for Pre‑1980 Multifamily Units
rules.requirement: Rent control applies to most units in multifamily properties built before 1980.
rules.coverage_conditions: multifamily properties built before 1980
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction for Pre‑1980 Multifamily Units
rules.requirement: Just‑cause eviction protections apply to most units in multifamily properties built before 1980.
rules.coverage_conditions: multifamily properties built before 1980
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

rules.title: Security‑Deposit Interest for Pre‑1980 Multifamily Units
rules.requirement: Security‑deposit interest provisions apply to most units in multifamily properties built before 1980.
rules.coverage_conditions: multifamily properties built before 1980
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

rules.title: Rent Control Exclusion for New Construction After June 1980
rules.requirement: Units built and receiving a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980 are not covered by rent control.
rules.coverage_conditions: units built after June 1980
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: New construction: units that were built and received a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980** Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction for New Construction After June 1980
rules.requirement: Just‑cause eviction protections apply to units built after June 1980 even though rent control does not.
rules.coverage_conditions: units built after June 1980
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: New construction: units that were built and received a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980** Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes

rules.title: Security‑Deposit Interest for New Construction After June 1980
rules.requirement: Security‑deposit interest provisions apply to units built after June 1980.
rules.coverage_conditions: units built after June 1980
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: New construction: units that were built and received a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980** Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes

rules.title: Rent Control Exemption for “Golden Duplex”
rules.requirement: Duplexes owner‑occupied on Dec 31 1979 with an owner living in one unit are exempt from rent control.
rules.coverage_conditions: duplex owner‑occupied on December 31, 1979
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: “Golden Duplex”: duplex that was owner-occupied on December 31, 1979, and currently has an owner living in one of the units Exempt No No No No

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Exemption for “Golden Duplex”
rules.requirement: The “Golden Duplex” exemption also excludes just‑cause eviction protections.
rules.coverage_conditions: duplex owner‑occupied on December 31, 1979
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: “Golden Duplex”: duplex that was owner-occupied on December 31, 1979, and currently has an owner living in one of the units Exempt No No No No

rules.title: Security‑Deposit Interest Exemption for “Golden Duplex”
rules.requirement: The “Golden Duplex” exemption also excludes security‑deposit interest provisions.
rules.coverage_conditions: duplex owner‑occupied on December 31, 1979
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: “Golden Duplex”: duplex that was owner-occupied on December 31, 1979, and currently has an owner living in one of the units Exempt No No No No

rules.title: Rent Control Exemption for ADU Owner‑Occupied Tenancies After Nov 7 2018
rules.requirement: Tenancies that started after Nov 7 2018 on properties with an ADU where either unit is owner‑occupied are exempt from rent control.
rules.coverage_conditions: tenancies started after November 7, 2018 on properties with an ADU and an owner‑occupied unit
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018, on properties where one unit is

rules.title: Fair Chance Tenant Selection – Criminal History Screening Restrictions
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding or with income‑restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy may not deny housing based on arrests without conviction, convictions that have been expunged or sealed, juvenile records, or convictions older than five years, except when the conviction directly relates to the housing sought or poses a safety risk.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development funding and/or land, or that have income‑restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought, an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to safety of others, or current criminal behavior.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, February 2017
rules.quoted_span: The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction: a) Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion programs, and similar non-convictions. b) Convictions that are subject to a form of judicial relief, such as expungement, sealing, and certificates for relief from disabilities. c) Juvenile records d) A conviction more than 5 years old.

rules.title: Fair Chance Tenant Selection – Credit Score Use Restriction
rules.requirement: Agents may not use an applicant's credit score to approve or deny housing applications; credit history may only be used in lieu of rental history when rental history is unavailable and must be considered alongside mitigating circumstances.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development funding and/or land, or that have income‑restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy, February 2017
rules.quoted_span: a) The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing applications. b) Property Managers may consider an applicant’s credit history, but such information may ONLY be used in lieu of rental history to determine an applicant’s ability to pay rent when rental history is not available.

rules.title: Prohibition on higher security deposits based on familial status
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not charge a higher security deposit to households with children.
rules.coverage_conditions: Households with children (familial status)
rules.quoted_span: Prohibiting housing providers from having conditions or rules that discriminate against households with children, such as charging a higher security deposit to households with children

rules.title: Prohibition on discriminatory tenant screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not screen prospective tenants in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic.
rules.coverage_conditions: All prospective tenants
rules.quoted_span: third-party such as a tenant screening company – in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic

rules.title: Prohibition on Use of Common Pricing Algorithms
rules.requirement: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade, and unlawful to coerce another person to adopt a price or commercial term recommended by such algorithm.
rules.coverage_conditions: All persons (excluding end consumers) in California
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not specified in the text
rules.interaction: Supersedes any local ordinances that permit algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: Just cause eviction after 12 months occupancy
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential rental unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without stating a statutory "just cause" in the written notice. Just cause includes specified at‑fault and no‑fault reasons listed in the statute.
rules.key_value: 12 months continuous occupancy; termination requires statutory just cause
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants who have continuously and lawfully occupied the residential real property for at least 12 months (or, when additional adult tenants are added, either all tenants have 12 months occupancy or one or more have 24 months occupancy)
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.interaction: Supersedes other statutes that would allow termination without just cause

rules.title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no‑fault just cause terminations
rules.requirement: When an owner terminates a tenancy for a no‑fault just cause, the owner must either provide the tenant with relocation assistance equal to one month of the tenant’s rent or waive the rent for the final month, and must notify the tenant of this right in the termination notice; failure to comply makes the termination notice void.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance = one month’s rent; rent waiver = one month’s rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any tenancy where just cause is required to terminate under this section.
rules.exemptions: (e)(1) Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; (e)(2) Housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended‑care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, or adult residential facilities; (e)(3) Dormitories owned by higher‑education institutions or K‑12 schools; (e)(4) Units where tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with owner‑occupied residence; (e)(5) Single‑family owner‑occupied residences (including ADUs, JADUs, and mobilehomes); (e)(6) Two‑unit buildings where owner occupies one unit; (e)(7) Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); (e)(8) Properties exempt because the owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member and tenants received the required exemption notice; (e)(9) Affordable‑housing units subject to deed or regulatory restrictions or housing subsidies; (i)(A) Residential property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause adopted on or before Sept 1 2019 (local ordinance applies); (i)(B) Local ordinance adopted after Sept 1 2019 that is more protective than this section (local ordinance applies).
rules.quoted_span: (d) (1) For a tenancy for which just cause is required to terminate the tenancy under subdivision (a), if an owner of residential real property issues a termination notice based on a no-fault just cause described in paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), the owner shall, regardless of the tenant’s income, at the owner’s option, do one of the following: (A) Assist the tenant to relocate by providing a direct payment to the tenant as described in paragraph (3). (B) Waive in writing the payment of rent for the final month of the tenancy, prior to the rent becoming due.
rules.interaction: Supersedes less‑protective local just‑cause ordinances; yields to any local ordinance that is more protective than this state provision.

rules.title: Rent increase cap for residential properties
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property may not increase the gross rent by more than 5 % plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 %, whichever is lower, over any 12‑month period, and may not apply more than two rent increases within that period.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential real property, including mobile‑home park units, except properties exempt under subdivision (d) (affordable housing, dormitories, rent‑controlled units, properties with a certificate of occupancy issued within the prior 15 years (unless a mobilehome), properties owned by REITs, corporations, or LLCs with corporate members, and owner‑occupied two‑unit buildings).
rules.exemptions: (d)(1)‑(6) list of exemptions covering affordable‑housing restrictions, dormitories, existing rent‑control, newer than 15 years, certain owner types, and owner‑occupied two‑unit structures.
rules.quoted_span: (a) (1) Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Statewide rent increase limitation
rules.requirement: Establishes statewide limitations on gross rental rate increases to address rent gouging during the housing crisis.
rules.quoted_span: (m) (1) The Legislature finds and declares that the unique circumstances of the current housing crisis require a statewide response to address rent gouging by establishing statewide limitations on gross rental rate increases.
rules.interaction: yields to local rent‑control authority under Chapter 2.7 (commencing with Section 1954.50)

rules.title: Maximum security deposit – one month rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit greater than one month’s rent, in addition to the first month’s rent, except as allowed by specific exceptions.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in California
rules.exemptions: Exceptions in subdivisions (c)(2), (c)(3), and (c)(5) of Civil Code §1950.5
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Advance payment of rent up to six months
rules.requirement: A landlord may require an advance payment of rent of at least six months when the lease term is six months or longer.
rules.key_value: not less than six months’ rent
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential leases with a term of six months or longer
rules.quoted_span: This subdivision does not prohibit an advance payment of not less than six months’ rent if the term of the lease is six months or longer.

rules.title: Two‑month security deposit for small landlords
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person or an LLC owned solely by natural persons and who owns no more than two residential rental properties (four units total) may demand a security deposit up to two months’ rent, in addition to the first month’s rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords who are natural persons or LLCs with all members natural persons, owning ≤2 properties and ≤4 units
rules.exemptions: Does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member (subparagraph (c)(5)(B))
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements: (i) The landlord is a natural person or a limited liability company in which all members are natural persons. (ii) The landlord owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.

rules.title: Service‑member higher security deposit disclosure and return
rules.requirement: For service‑member tenants, a landlord must provide a written statement of any higher security amount and the reason before lease signing, and must return the additional amount within six months if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.key_value: return within six months of residency
rules.coverage_conditions: Service‑member tenants of residential rental units
rules.quoted_span: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged. The additional amount of security shall be returned to the tenant after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears for any rent due during that period.

rules.title: Security‑deposit return timeline and itemized statement
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after a tenant vacates, the landlord must provide an itemized statement of deductions and return any remaining security deposit by personal delivery or check (or electronically if originally paid electronically).
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in California
rules.quoted_span:
lease, the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant as follows:
(A)

rules.title: Security Deposit Return and Itemized Accounting
rules.requirement: When a tenancy ends, the landlord must return the remaining security deposit together with an itemized statement of deductions, delivered by personal delivery or first‑class mail, postage prepaid, or by electronic means if the tenant agrees in writing.
rules.exemptions: If the total deductions for repairs and cleaning are $125 or less, the landlord may omit the detailed documentation. A tenant‑signed waiver of these rights can also exempt the landlord from providing the full documentation.
rules.quoted_span: (i) Subject to subparagraph (C), and except as provided by clause (ii), the landlord shall furnish the itemized statement by personal delivery or first-class mail, postage prepaid.

rules.title: Prohibition of Nonrefundable Security Deposits
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not contain any provision that characterizes a security deposit as “nonrefundable.”
rules.quoted_span: (n) A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Deduction Limit for Repairs and Cleaning
rules.requirement: If the total deductions for repairs and cleaning do not exceed $125, the landlord is not required to provide the detailed documentation normally required with the itemized statement.
rules.quoted_span: (A) The deductions for repairs and cleaning together do not exceed one hundred twenty-five dollars ($125).

rules.title: Maximum application screening fee
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee of no more than $30 per applicant, and the fee may be adjusted each year based on the Consumer Price Index.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.

rules.title: Application screening process requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide written screening criteria with the application, consider applications in the order received, approve the first applicant who meets the criteria, and may not charge a fee until the application is actually considered.
rules.quoted_span: Completed applications are considered, as provided for in the landlord’s established screening criteria, in the order in which the completed applications were received. The landlord’s screening criteria shall be provided to the applicant in writing together with the application form.

rules.title: Credit‑history screening must offer alternative evidence
rules.requirement: When a landlord uses a credit‑history check in a rental application, they must also give the applicant the option to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay, and must allow reasonable time to submit that evidence.
rules.exemptions: Owners may still request employment verification, landlord references, or identity verification.
rules.quoted_span:
Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

rules.title: Applicant selection standards must be reasonable and applied uniformly
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers, and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to select applicants, but the standard must be applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental housing covered by the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance
rules.exemptions: Exempt for 2‑family dwellings when the owner lives there
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants. Tenant selection may be based on: an applicant's ability to pay the rent an applicant's ability to take care of the apartment and to respect the rights of others NOTE: there is an exemption for 2-family dwellings, when the owner lives there

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may terminate a tenancy only for the listed just causes; at‑fault evictions provide no relocation assistance, while non‑at‑fault evictions require relocation assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in LA not covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance; applies to buildings newer than October 1 1978 and to single‑family dwellings; tenant must have occupied the unit at least six months or have an expired lease.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner’s roommate, certain cooperatives, some non‑profit homeless facilities, short‑term substance‑abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Housing Department, Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span:
The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
In order to apply to a tenancy, it requires that the tenant either has lived in the same unit for at least six months or that their original lease expired, whichever comes first.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date of the ordinance is not stated in the source document.

rules.title: Non‑payment eviction restriction
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind on rent unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent for the unit’s bedroom size.
rules.coverage_conditions: All RSO & JCO rental units
rules.citation: Los Angeles Housing Department, Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) rent increase limits
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the regional cost‑of‑living change, or 10% whichever is lower; for Aug 1 2024–Jul 31 2025 the maximum increase is 8.9%, and for Aug 1 2023–Jul 31 2024 it was 8.8%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units built more than 15 years ago, unless exempt by deed, regulatory restriction, dormitory status, owner‑occupied second unit, or single‑family home not owned by a corporation/trust/LLC with corporate member and with written notice of exemption.
rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years, units with affordability restrictions, certain dormitories, two‑unit properties where the second unit is owner‑occupied, exempt single‑family homes meeting specific ownership and notice criteria, and units already covered by the City’s RSO.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Housing Department, Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: nnual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower).
rules.interaction: State law supersedes city rent‑increase regulations; JCO defers to AB 1482 for rent‑increase limits.

rules.title: Prohibition of utility percentage increase
rules.requirement: Landlords may not include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.key_value: no additional percentage increase for utilities
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all RSO‑covered rental units.
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.

rules.title: Additional tenant vs. dependent rent increase
rules.requirement: An additional 10% increase for a dependent is prohibited, but a 10% increase for an additional tenant (not a dependent) is allowed within 60 days of learning of the new tenant.
rules.key_value: no 10% increase for dependent; 10% allowed for additional tenant
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all RSO‑covered rental units.
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

rules.title: Relocation assistance required for no‑fault evictions under RSO/JCO
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay relocation assistance and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with the Los Angeles Housing Department before evicting a tenant for a no‑fault reason under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: Prohibition on discriminatory inducement in housing transactions
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for any person to induce, attempt to induce, prevent, or attempt to prevent the sale, purchase, or rental of any dwelling by making representations or unrequested contacts that relate to a person's protected characteristics such as age, race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, economic level, disability, or having a child.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person attempting to induce, prevent, or solicit the sale, purchase, or rental of any dwelling.
rules.quoted_span: For any person to directly or indirectly induce, attempt to induce, prevent, or attempt to prevent the sale, purchase, or rental of any dwelling or dwellings by: (a) implicit or explicit representations regarding the entry or prospective entry into the neighborhood of a person or persons of a particular age, race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, or economic level or a handicapped person, or a person having a child, or implicit or explicit representations regarding the effects or consequences of any such entry or prospective entry; (b) unrequested contact or communication with any person or persons, initiated by any means, for the purpose of so inducing or attempting to induce the sale, purchase, or rental of any dwelling or dwellings when he knew or, in the exercise of reasonable care, should have known that such unrequested solicitation would reasonably be associated by the persons solicited with the entry into the neighborhood of a person or persons of a particular age, race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, or economic level or a handicapped person, or a person having a child;

rules.title: Security deposit limits and optional fee in lieu of deposit
rules.requirement: A landlord may only require a security deposit equal to one month’s rent and may, if authorized by regulations, accept an optional fee in lieu of the deposit that cannot exceed one month’s rent. The landlord must provide a receipt, a written condition statement, and hold the deposit in a separate interest‑bearing account with interest paid at 5% per year.
rules.key_value: max deposit = 1 month’s rent; optional fee max = 1 month’s rent

rules.title: Security‑deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: If a landlord holds a security deposit for one year or longer, the landlord must pay the tenant interest at 5% per year (or the lesser amount actually earned) each year of the tenancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security deposit held for one year or longer from the start of the tenancy
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.

rules.title: Security‑deposit return and permissible deductions
rules.requirement: A landlord must return the security deposit (or balance) within 30 days after tenancy ends, and may deduct only unpaid rent or water charges, unpaid tax‑escalation amounts, or reasonable repair costs not covered by normal wear and tear.
rules.key_value: Return within 30 days; deductions limited to rent, tax escalation, repair costs
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential leases covered by this section
rules.exemptions: No deduction for damage listed in the pre‑lease condition statement or tenant‑provided damage list unless new damage is proven

The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;  provided, however, that the lessor may deduct from such security deposit for the following:
(i) any unpaid rent or water charges

rules.title: Transfer of security deposit upon landlord’s interest transfer
rules.requirement: When a landlord transfers his interest in the rental unit, he must transfer the security deposit and accrued interest to the successor, who must notify the tenant in writing within 45 days of the transfer.
rules.key_value: Successor must notify tenant within 45 days
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies whenever the lessor transfers his interest (sale, assignment, death, bankruptcy, etc.)
rules.exemptions: Granting a mortgage is not a transfer; city or town acquiring title, foreclosing mortgagee, or mortgagee in possession are exempt from liability

rules.title: Triple‑damage penalty for security‑deposit violations
rules.requirement: If a landlord fails to deposit the security funds, provide the required itemized damage list, or return the deposit (with interest) within the required time, the tenant is entitled to three times the deposit amount plus 5% annual interest, plus costs and attorney’s fees.

rules.title: Criminal Record Screening Restrictions
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not inquire about an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer, and may not evaluate applicants based on arrests, expunged, pardoned, vacated, juvenile, or sealed records. After a conditional offer, only convictions for serious offenses within specified time windows may be considered.
rules.key_value: 6‑year window for 1st‑degree indictable offenses, 4‑year for 2nd/3rd‑degree, 1‑year for 4th‑degree; plus specific violent/sex‑offender crimes always allowed
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental dwelling units except owner‑occupied premises of four or fewer units
rules.exemptions: May consider drug‑related methamphetamine manufacturing in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex‑offender registration requirements
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on any of the following types of criminal records: (1) arrests or charges that have not resulted in a criminal conviction; (2) expunged convictions; (3) convictions erased through executive pardon; (4) vacated and otherwise legally nullified convictions; (5) juvenile adjudications of delinquency; and (6) records that have been sealed.

rules.title: Disclosure Requirement Before Accepting Application Fees
rules.requirement: Before accepting any application fee, a housing provider must provide a written disclosure stating whether criminal history will be considered and informing the applicant of their right to dispute or provide evidence of inaccuracies or rehabilitation.
rules.coverage_conditions: All applicants for rental dwelling units (excluding owner‑occupied premises of four or fewer units)
rules.quoted_span: Prior to accepting any application fee, a housing provider shall disclose in writing to the applicant: (1) Whether the eligibility criteria of the housing provider include the review and consideration of criminal history; and (2) A statement that the applicant, pursuant to subsection a. of this section, may provide evidence demonstrating inaccuracies within the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors.

rules.title: Residential Rental Property Application Fee Limit
rules.requirement: A landlord or its agent may not charge an application or similar fee exceeding $50 for a residential rental lease or sublease, except for certain exemptions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental property applications for dwelling purposes in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: (1) a dwelling unit located in a one‑family or two‑family dwelling that is offered for rent; (2) a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: a. A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.

rules.title: Just cause requirement for lease non‑renewal
rules.requirement: Landlords may not fail to renew a residential lease unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to residential rental properties except owner‑occupied two‑ or three‑family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units
rules.exemptions: owner‑occupied two‑ or three‑family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units are exempt
rules.quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

rules.title: Security deposit return after lease termination due to domestic violence
rules.requirement: Landlords must make the security deposit and any earned interest available within 15 business days after termination and must notify the tenant in writing within three business days of where and when to pick it up.
rules.key_value: return within 15 business days; notice within 3 business days
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential leases terminated under the New Jersey Safe Housing Act (domestic violence)
rules.exemptions: None specified for this rule
rules.quoted_span: Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s agent. In addition, within three business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of when and where the tenant can pick up the security deposit.

rules.requirement: A landlord may collect a security deposit no greater than one and one‑half times one month’s rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in New Jersey
rules.exemptions: Seasonal‑use rentals are exempt
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: Maximum total due at lease inception
rules.requirement: At lease start a landlord may not require more than two and one‑half times the monthly rent, including the first month’s rent and the security deposit.

rules.requirement: Any yearly increase to a security deposit may not exceed ten percent of the current deposit amount.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in New Jersey
rules.exemptions: Seasonal‑use rentals are exempt
rules.quoted_span: Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: Pet deposit combined limit

rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in New Jersey
rules.exemptions: Seasonal‑use rentals are exempt
rules.quoted_span: A landlord may not charge a pet security deposit if it exceeds one and one-half times one month’s rent when combined with the regular security deposit.

rules.title: Return of security deposit after tenancy termination
rules.requirement: A landlord must return the security deposit, plus earned interest less lawful deductions, to the tenant within 30 days after the tenancy ends (or after re‑renting the unit when the lease is broken).
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in New Jersey
rules.exemptions: Seasonal‑use rentals are exempt
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Double damages for late return
rules.requirement: If a landlord fails to return the security deposit within the required 30‑day period, the tenant may sue for twice the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in New Jersey
rules.exemptions: Seasonal‑use rentals are exempt
rules.quoted_span: If a landlord fails to return the security deposit within 30 days, or the tenant disagrees with the amount deducted, the tenant may sue for double the amount of the security deposit that the tenant contends was wrongfully withheld.

rules.title: Rapid return after displacement
rules.requirement: When a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit within five business days, and must inform the tenant within three business days where the deposit can be collected.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in New Jersey
rules.exemptions: Seasonal‑use rentals are exempt

having received notice of the displacement, the landlord must let the tenant know where the

rules.title: Rent increase notice and unconscionability requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must give proper written notice of lease termination and rent increase, and the increase may not be unconscionable; it must comply with any municipal rent‑control ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt for 30 years (N.J.S.A. 2A:42‑84.5); subsidized housing and HUD‑financed units are also exempt; conversions to condos/co‑ops cannot increase rent to cover conversion costs (N.J.S.A. 2A:18‑61.31).

rules.title: Charging for credit report costs
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge tenants the actual cost of obtaining a credit report used in the rental application.
rules.coverage_conditions: Prospective residential tenants.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the report.

rules.title: Disclosure of adverse credit reporting source
rules.requirement: If an application is denied based on a credit report, the landlord must give the applicant the name, address, and telephone number of the reporting agency.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applicants denied due to credit report.
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant’s  application is denied due their credit report, the landlord must provide the tenant with the name, address, and telephone number of the credit reporting or screening agency that supplied the negative report (15 U.S.C.A. § 1681m).

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – Good cause required for eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords may evict only for good cause; each cause (except nonpayment of rent) must be described in a written notice to the tenant before filing an eviction action.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties including single‑family homes, mobile homes, apartments, complexes, rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to two‑ or three‑unit owner‑occupied premises.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). There are several grounds for a good cause eviction. Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord in a written notice to the tenant.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not specified in source text.

rules.title: Constructive eviction – security deposit return
rules.requirement: If a landlord is negligent and the tenant successfully claims constructive eviction, the tenant is entitled to the return of the security deposit and is not liable for remaining rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when a landlord fails to maintain vital facilities, leading to a constructive eviction claim.

the landlord is found to be negligent in maintaining the rental unit, the tenant is entitled t

rules.title: Failure to Pay Rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant immediately for nonpayment of rent; no notice is required except for tenants in federally subsidized housing, who must receive a 14‑day notice before filing an eviction suit.
rules.key_value: no notice required; 14‑day notice for federally subsidized housing
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to all residential rental units; excludes hotel guests, motel guests, guest houses, and units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member
rules.exemptions: federally subsidized housing requires a 14‑day notice
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may immediately take legal action to have the tenant evicted. The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. I f the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing a 14-day notice must be given before filing a suite for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a)).

rules.title: Disorderly Conduct
rules.requirement: If a tenant continues disorderly conduct after a written notice to cease, the landlord may file for eviction, but must serve a Notice to Quit at least three days before filing the suit.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least 3 days prior
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to all residential rental units
rules.quoted_span: If after given written Notice to Cease disorderly conduct, the tenant continues the disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

rules.requirement: If a tenant substantially violates the landlord’s reasonable rules after written notice, the landlord may evict after serving a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing the suit, and the notice must be given on or before the start of a new month.

A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for this type of eviction.

rules.requirement: A landlord may evict for serious health‑safety violations or when the property is removed from the rental market after serving a Notice to Quit at least three months before filing the suit; relocation assistance must be provided.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least 3 months prior
rules.coverage_conditions: applies to all residential rental units
rules.quoted_span:
A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit 
for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

rules.title: Conversion to Condominium, Cooperative, or Fee Simple Eviction Notice
rules.requirement: A landlord must serve a Notice to Quit at least three years before filing an eviction suit when converting the property, and may not take legal action until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit ≥ 3 years before filing suit
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when a rental building or mobile home park is being converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee‑simple ownership of two or more units.
rules.exemptions: Senior citizen or disabled tenants with protected tenancy status under the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act of 1992 are exempt.
rules.quoted_span:
ved on the tenant at least 
three years before filing a suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease 
expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(k)).

rules.title: Tenancy After Conversion Eviction Notice
rules.requirement: A landlord must serve a Notice to Quit at least two months before filing an eviction suit after a conversion, and may not take legal action until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit ≥ 2 months before filing suit
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants whose initial tenancy began after the master deed or cooperative agreement was recorded when the owner seeks personal occupancy or sale of the unit.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(l)).

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Immunity
rules.requirement: No eviction action may be brought against senior citizen or disabled tenants with protected tenancy status during the protected period, unless the agency terminates that status.
rules.coverage_conditions: Senior citizens and disabled tenants covered by the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act of 1992.
rules.exemptions: If the protected tenancy status is terminated or the protected period expires, the exemption ends.
rules.citation: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act of 1992
rules.quoted_span: No action for possession shall be brought against a senior citizen tenant or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status pursuant to the “Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act of 1992,” as long as the agency has not terminated the protected tenancy status or the protected tenancy period has not expired.

rules.title: Owner‑Occupied Two‑ and Three‑Family Eviction Notice Requirements
rules.requirement: For at‑will or year‑to‑year tenancies a three‑month notice to quit is required; for month‑to‑month tenancies a one‑month notice is required; a three‑day notice is required for disorderly or lease‑violation causes.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in landlord‑occupied two‑ or three‑family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: No notice required when eviction is for non‑payment of rent.
rules.quoted_span:
three-day written Notice to Quit is 
required for any of the causes described as disorderly, destructive or violative of written rules or 
lease provisions (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2(a)).

rules.title: Rooming and Boarding House Eviction Procedures
rules.requirement: Owners must follow the general good‑cause and notice requirements of the Eviction Law and must give at least three working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board before commencing an eviction action.
rules.key_value: ≥3 working days notice to County Welfare Board
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of rooming or boarding houses (buildings with ≥2 unrelated living units without private kitchens/baths).
rules.exemptions: Exceptions listed in the Rooming and Boarding House Act (e.g., hotels with >85% temporary occupancy, dormitories, etc.).
rules.quoted_span:
Affairs, 
require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements 
of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 
5:27-3.3(c)). There is a further requirement that the owner give at least three (3) working days’ 
notice to the County Welfare Board before starting the eviction action for any resident  (N.J.A.C. 
5:26-3.4(c)).
rules.interaction: supplements state eviction law
